definition: Dense vector representations of whole sentences that place semantically similar texts near each other.
details: Dense vector representations of whole sentences that place semantically similar texts near each other. Produced by models such as Sentence-BERT, they power retrieval, clustering, and semantic search.

explainer.lead: Sentence embeddings are dense vectors for whole sentences that place semantically similar texts near each other. They matter because they enable retrieval and semantic search without exact keyword matching.

tiers.eli5: Imagine giving every sentence a set of coordinates so that sentences with similar meanings end up close together on a map; that's what sentence embeddings do.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers produce sentence embeddings with models like Sentence-BERT and use them for retrieval, clustering, and semantic search. A pitfall is that embedding quality degrades on out-of-domain text, and high-dimensional vectors can be costly to store and search at scale.
tiers.paperLevel: Sentence embeddings are dense vector representations of whole sentences that place semantically similar texts near each other, produced by models such as Sentence-BERT. Their effectiveness is limited by the training data and by the choice of similarity metric.

explainer.example: A customer support system embeds each FAQ entry; when a user asks 'How do I reset my password?', it retrieves the closest FAQ vector even if the wording differs.
